slice.leaf: deterministic per-parent idempotency-key model for checkpoint-first/pointer-last persistence
slice.question: Can repeated failed or stale retries from one frozen parent be prevented from creating an unbounded sequence of distinct orphan checkpoints without overwriting current authority or auto-adopting mismatched content?

public_source.name: GitHub REST repository contents endpoint
public_source.relevant_semantics: Repository contents writes distinguish create/update behavior; replacing an existing file requires its current blob SHA, and conflicting content operations can fail. The tested protocol therefore treats candidate creation as create-if-absent and forbids retry-time replacement of an existing candidate path.

model.parent: the exact current LATEST blob SHA frozen before candidate construction
model.next_revision: fixed as parent logical_revision + 1; retries may not choose an arbitrary new revision while the same parent remains current
model.candidate_path: a deterministic role-local path derived only from K
model.payload_rule: semantic payload is canonicalized deterministically; volatile invocation timestamps, random IDs and retry counters are excluded from the candidate bytes or deterministically derived from K
model.collision_rule: if path is absent, create once; if path exists and bytes exactly match, treat as idempotent existing candidate; if bytes differ, stop diagnostically for this invocation and never overwrite, rename, content-hash-fork or auto-adopt the existing candidate
model.authority_rule: LATEST may advance only by CAS from the frozen parent blob to the exact matching candidate; CAS failure leaves at most that one candidate orphan for K and cannot mutate current authority

candidates.A_unique_per_attempt: Every retry chooses a fresh path or retry UUID.
candidates.B_deterministic_parent_revision: One path per fixed parent LATEST blob plus parent+1 revision, deterministic normalized payload, create-if-absent, exact-match retry, mismatch diagnostic, pointer-last CAS.
candidates.C_content_hash_fork: Path includes payload/content hash so semantically divergent retries can coexist.

steps: LATEST remains at parent p/revision r
repeat N times from unchanged p
deterministic_traces.A: FAIL: N retries can create N distinct orphan paths.
deterministic_traces.B: PASS: every retry addresses the same K/path; after the first create, exact matching retries reuse that candidate, so distinct orphan count attributable to this parent is at most one.
deterministic_traces.C: FAIL if payload can vary: distinct content hashes create multiple orphan paths from the same parent.

steps: two writers freeze the same parent p
both compute identical K and canonical bytes
the other observes the same existing bytes
both attempt LATEST CAS from p
deterministic_traces.A: duplicate candidate files may be created before the pointer race resolves
deterministic_traces.B: PASS: one candidate path exists; at most one pointer CAS from p can establish authority, and the losing CAS cannot mutate the newer pointer
deterministic_traces.C: no advantage over B for identical bytes

steps: two writers freeze p but produce different candidate bytes
first writer creates deterministic K path
deterministic_traces.A: can preserve both divergent attempts as separate orphans
deterministic_traces.B: PASS safety / diagnostic liveness: second writer must not overwrite or adopt; current authority remains unchanged unless the creator later wins the parent CAS. This exposes deterministic payload normalization as a required liveness condition.
deterministic_traces.C: FAIL orphan bound: divergent hashes deliberately create more than one path for the same parent

steps: LATEST advances from p to p2
a stale writer based on p creates or finds K(p,r+1)
stale writer attempts CAS expecting p
deterministic_traces.A: each repeated stale attempt can leave another orphan
deterministic_traces.B: PASS: stale CAS is rejected; repeated stale retries from the same p reuse the same deterministic path, so they cannot create a second orphan for that parent/revision
deterministic_traces.C: payload variation can again create multiple stale orphans

steps: candidate path is deterministically namespaced by parent/revision
existing candidate path is treated immutable
LATEST update remains the only authority-changing operation
deterministic_traces.B: PASS within model: retries never use update/replace on candidate files and never write through the current LATEST target path; a mismatched collision is diagnostic-only, so a reachable checkpoint is not overwritten

A_unique_per_attempt.safety: authority CAS can remain safe, but orphan creation is unbounded under repeated interruption from a stuck parent
A_unique_per_attempt.success_probability: high per attempt but poor retry storage behavior

B_deterministic_parent_revision.orphan_bound_same_parent: PASS: at most one distinct candidate path for a fixed current parent because next_revision is fixed to parent+1
B_deterministic_parent_revision.expected_completion_time: one candidate create/read plus one pointer CAS; retry after interruption is exact-match reuse rather than another write
B_deterministic_parent_revision.success_probability: high when payload normalization is deterministic; intentionally diagnostic on divergent bytes
B_deterministic_parent_revision.integration_cost: medium; requires canonical payload normalization and strict create/exact-match/mismatch rules
B_deterministic_parent_revision.quota_fragility: none beyond lightweight repository transport; no hosted compute, artifact service, finite credit or external executor

C_content_hash_fork.safety: can avoid overwrite but does not bound retry-created orphans
C_content_hash_fork.success_probability: high for preserving divergent outputs, which is precisely the unwanted behavior for this persistence protocol

slice.falsification_test: The design would be falsified if one frozen parent p with fixed next_revision=r+1 could produce two distinct candidate paths, if a mismatched retry could overwrite or auto-adopt existing candidate bytes, or if a stale writer could advance LATEST after the parent changed. None occurs under candidate B's stated rules.
slice.candidate_revision: Promote deterministic parent+next-revision candidate identity as the preferred orphan-creation control for the tested pointer model. It complements r173 reachability retention: creation is capped at one candidate per stuck parent/revision, while later reachability-plus-two-confirmed-generation cleanup can reclaim a persistent orphan after pointer progress resumes. Keep never-delete retention as fail-safe. Do not use content-hash forking for retry identity.
slice.tested_scope: Deterministic role-local model with one CAS-updated LATEST pointer, immutable candidate/checkpoint files, parent logical revision available in LATEST, next revision fixed to parent+1, canonical deterministic candidate bytes, and create-if-absent/exact-match collision handling. Traces cover repeated pre-CAS interruption, same-parent concurrency with matching and mismatching bytes, stale writer after valid advance, and overwrite guard. No live production candidate collision was induced; no claim is made for multi-pointer authorities, noncanonical/nondeterministic semantic payloads, or transports that permit silent overwrite without a precondition.
slice.negative_result: A deterministic path alone is insufficient if retry payload bytes contain volatile metadata: it bounds the number of paths but can turn benign retries into permanent mismatch diagnostics. Canonical payload determinism is therefore part of the mechanism, not an implementation detail.

phase1_constraints.quota_note: The slice uses scheduled-Chat reasoning plus lightweight repository state transport only. It requires no hosted runner, Codespaces, artifact/LFS/package quota, external model/API credit, protected-primary action, or manual user execution.

slice.conflict_check: Only frozen sanitized controls, own LATEST/r173 state and one public GitHub repository-contents source were used. No O/O-derived, other-worker, downstream, legacy, aggregate-ledger, other-role receipt/config, scheduler or protected-primary semantic input was read or mutated.

frontier: Test interruption and rate-limit recovery for the deterministic parent/revision candidate without same-run retry: candidate create succeeds but pointer update is unavailable; next invocation must reconstruct the same K, exact-match bytes, and attempt only the pointer CAS, while an authority change must force a stale-writer diagnostic rather than adoption.
Then test whether canonical payload normalization can be separated into immutable semantic bytes plus non-authoritative receipt metadata without reintroducing duplicate candidate identities.
exact_continuation: Next invocation, after manifest/RUN_LIFECYCLE-first bootstrap and exact authority freeze, read LATEST and r174 only as needed, then execute exactly one bounded interruption/rate-limit recovery model leaf. Simulate candidate-create success followed by pointer-write unavailability and normal return with no same-run retry; on the next invocation require reconstruction of the same K and exact bytes, then allow only (a) pointer CAS if the frozen parent is still current, (b) exact-match no-op if the pointer already targets that candidate, or (c) stale/authority-mismatch diagnostic if LATEST changed. Falsify if recovery writes a second candidate path, silently replaces mismatched bytes, or adopts a stale candidate after parent change.
